links.outcome: AUC and specificity on external Turkish and Belgian cohorts versus development performance
links.effect: Class III AUC 0.902 (Turkish) vs 0.835 (non-European), difference 0.066, p=0.029; specificity fell from 0.766 to 0.697. Class I vs II AUC 0.875 vs 0.723, difference 0.152, p<0.001.
links.quote: AUC was lower in the non-European cohort for all three models in both tasks.

links.effect: AUC lower in the Belgian non-European cohort than the Turkish external cohort in both tasks (0.066 and 0.152 differences); sensitivity was similar across sets (all adjusted p>0.7).
links.quote: The observed performance differences are consistent with a population-specific generalizability effect rather than model-specific failure and support mandatory external validation on target populations before clinical deployment.

links.outcome: Sensitivity by age subgroup (children vs adults) in external cohorts
links.effect: Sensitivity lower in children (0.71 to 0.80) than adults (0.89 to 0.90) across both external cohorts.
links.quote: A subgroup analysis showed lower sensitivity in children than adults across both cohorts (0.71 to 0.80 versus 0.89 to 0.90).

screen.reason: The study conducts an external validation of an image-based screening machine learning tool across diverse cohorts and subgroups, but does not test an organizational deployment practice or safeguard intervention.
